notes: Read all 149 source lines before porting. globalProgress.ts is a singleton 'is the app busy?' progress controller — pure non-visual controller/utility code (contract rule 6). It touches no DOM, no browser HTML elements, no Recharts/Leaflet, and no web UI components; the only platform primitives are setInterval/clearInterval, Set, Array.from, and Math.*, all of which React Native provides on the global scope, so the logic ports 1:1 with no behavioral change.

L1-25 module JSDoc block preserved as `//` line comments (matching the sibling closestRoute/broadcast parity headers): the controller purpose, the two callers (<SuspenseProgressBoundary>, useGlobalProgress), the start/stop pairing concurrency contract, the StrictMode double-invoke idempotency note, and the asymptotic-trickle-toward-80% (NProgress-style) snap-back behavior. A '## Native conversion (contract rule 6)' section was appended documenting that setInterval/clearInterval/Set/Array.from/Math are RN-provided and that the <TopProgress>/<SuspenseProgressBoundary>/useGlobalProgress/main.tsx/window.error references are web-surface PROSE only, not imports or runtime deps.
L27 `export type GlobalProgressListener = (active: boolean, progress: number) => void` ported verbatim (semicolon added per .prettierrc.js).
L28-34 the three exported tuning constants ported verbatim with their `/** */` JSDoc: TRICKLE_TARGET=80 (L29-30), TRICKLE_INITIAL=8 (L31-32), TRICKLE_INTERVAL_MS=120 (L33-34).

L36-39 module-level mutable state ported verbatim: `let activeCount = 0`, `let progress = 0`, `let trickleHandle: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null` (the ReturnType<typeof setInterval> typing is the established native pattern, mirroring api/client.ts's `ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>` — works on RN where the handle is a number/Timeout without pulling in the DOM lib), and `const listeners = new Set<GlobalProgressListener>()`.

L41-53 publish() ported verbatim: `active = activeCount > 0`, the Array.from(listeners) snapshot (with the 'listeners may add/remove during dispatch' comment), the per-listener try { fn(active, progress) } catch {} guard, and the full catch-block comment about main.tsx/window.error keeping the channel alive. no-empty is disabled in @react-native eslint config and the catch retains its explanatory comment regardless.

L55-69 startTrickle() ported verbatim: the `if (trickleHandle !== null) return` re-entry guard (braces added; @react-native curly rule is unset and prettier preserves either form — behavior identical), setInterval at TRICKLE_INTERVAL_MS, the activeCount===0 -> stopTrickle()+return self-cancel, the progress>=TRICKLE_TARGET early return, `remaining = TRICKLE_TARGET - progress`, the 'move 15% of remaining each tick, Math.max(1,...) forward-motion floor, never crosses target' comment, and `progress = Math.min(TRICKLE_TARGET, progress + Math.max(1, remaining * 0.15))` (prettier wrapped the Math.min args across lines because the single-line form is 82 cols > 80 print width; the expression and result are byte-for-byte equivalent), then publish().
L71-76 stopTrickle() ported verbatim: the trickleHandle !== null guard, clearInterval(trickleHandle), and `trickleHandle = null`.

L78-101 start() ported verbatim: `activeCount++` (no-plusplus is disabled in the @react-native config, so the ++ is kept exactly as source), the activeCount===1 first-start branch (progress = TRICKLE_INITIAL; startTrickle()), publish(), the closure-local `let stopped = false` guard with its full StrictMode/underflow-prevention comment, and the returned idempotent `stop()` (early return if stopped, set stopped=true, `activeCount = Math.max(0, activeCount - 1)`, and on reaching 0: stopTrickle()+progress=0+publish()).

L103-115 subscribe() ported verbatim: listeners.add(fn), the immediate replay `fn(activeCount > 0, progress)` inside try/catch with the 'listener mounted while bar active must not miss the active edge' comment and the `/* see publish */` empty-catch marker, and the returned unsubscribe `() => { listeners.delete(fn) }`.
L117-120 the exported `globalProgress = { start, subscribe } as const` public surface ported verbatim — start and subscribe are the only two public channel operations.

L122-128 the '── Test-only helpers ──' banner + the comment explaining the double-underscore convention (production app must never import these; titleStore/errorReporter precedent) preserved verbatim.
L130-135 __resetGlobalProgressForTests() ported verbatim: activeCount=0, progress=0, stopTrickle(), listeners.clear() — clears state AND timers between test cases.

L137-149 __getGlobalProgressStateForTests() ported verbatim including the inline return-type literal { activeCount; progress; listeners; trickling } and the returned snapshot { activeCount, progress, listeners: listeners.size, trickling: trickleHandle !== null }.
No browser-only behavior to stub (contract rule 7 not triggered): every primitive used is part of the React Native global runtime. No explicit unavailable-state needed.
